analysis:
## Technical analysis (June 27 UTC — post-close 20:05 UTC)

**Crypto.com MCP confirmed final close data:** Open $60,104.10 / High $60,947.94 / Low $59,876.86 / Close $60,241.43. Full-session volume: 1,352.64 BTC ($81.5M). Change +$138.33 (+0.23%) from June 26 close.

**Day 5 exit gate CONFIRMED.** Five consecutive UTC closes below $63,500: June 23 ($62,724.97) → June 24 ($61,078.01) → June 25 ($59,795.45) → June 26 ($60,103.10) → June 27 ($60,241.43). The distribution phase is now five sessions deep.

**Shooting star candle — $61,000 rejection.** The June 27 session printed a shooting star: open $60,104 → high $60,948 → close $60,241. Bulls pushed to $60,948 intraday (testing the $61,000 round number resistance) and were overwhelmed by sellers, with price closing $707 below the session high. This is a single-candle bearish reversal signal at overhead resistance. The failure to close above $60,500 on the highest intraday print of the past two sessions confirms $61,000–$62,000 is strong resistance.

**Trend read:** BTC is in a confirmed intermediate downtrend (5 consecutive exit-gate closes). Price is trading below all key moving averages with declining session highs: June 25 high $61,967 → June 26 high $60,767 → June 27 high $60,948 (marginal uptick in high, but still well below $62,000 gate). The two-session stabilization ($60,103–$60,241 close range) suggests temporary equilibrium in the $59,800–$61,000 band, not structural reversal.

**Strongest resistance:** $62,000 (★ re-entry gate — two consecutive UTC closes required). This level is confirmed by: (1) the formal re-entry framework gate; (2) the June 25 session high $61,967 (failed at this level); (3) the shooting star rejection at $60,948 suggests sellers step in well before $62,000; (4) the entire June 23–27 distribution phase has been unable to close above this level.

**Strongest support:** $60,000 (★ round number / heaviest put OI). This level is confirmed by: (1) June 27 close $60,241 held $241 above $60,000; (2) June 26 close $60,103 held $103 above $60,000; (3) the $60,000 strike is the heaviest concentration of put open interest in the July expiry; (4) two consecutive closes above $60,000 suggest buyers defending this level. Below $60,000, the next structural support is $59,877 (June 27 session low), then $58,325 (June 26 low), then $58,100 (June 25 low).

**Volume analysis:** Full-session volume 1,352.64 BTC ($81.5M) — approximately 75% below a typical weekday ($250–400M). The low Saturday volume means the $60,948 intraday high was a thin-market push without institutional conviction. Volume did not spike on the move toward $61,000 — confirming the rejection was not a high-conviction selling event but rather thin-market dynamics. Volume is diverging bearishly from the higher-low price structure: price made a higher low, but volume is declining (Saturday < Wednesday–Friday sessions), suggesting weak demand, not accumulation.

**Higher-low basing signal:** Three consecutive higher lows are now confirmed: $58,100 (June 25) → $58,325 (June 26) → $59,877 (June 27). This is the ONLY constructive technical development in the five-session distribution phase. It suggests downside capitulation may be slowing. However, higher lows alone cannot activate the re-entry clock — two consecutive UTC closes ABOVE $62,000 are required.

**What would invalidate the bear read:** A June 29 UTC close above $62,000 combined with IBIT net daily inflows > $100M would activate Day 1 of the re-entry clock. A sustained June 29 close above $63,500 would exit the exit-gate sequence and would require a full re-assessment of the distribution thesis.
